questions.text: Tell me about a time you prevented a stockout that would have impacted sales.

key_points: How you identified the risk early (forecast vs stock position)
Action taken: expedite, reorder, transfer stock
Sales or service level impact avoided
strong_answer_signals: Root cause addressed in replenishment model

questions.text: Describe a time you significantly reduced excess or obsolete inventory.

key_points: Identified slow-movers via coverage and days-on-hand analysis
Levers: promotions, markdown, liquidation, transfers
Inventory value freed and write-off reduction
avoid: No root cause fix to buying process

questions.text: Tell me about a time you improved forecast accuracy for a product or category.

key_points: Baseline: what the MAPE/bias was before
Improvement levers: better statistical model, market intelligence, promotion uplift
Accuracy improvement and downstream benefit
avoid: Improved gut feel with no metric

questions.text: Describe how you managed inventory across a product lifecycle, introduction through discontinuation.

key_points: Launch: initial buy, safety stock, channel fill estimation
Growth/maturity: replenishment model tuning
End-of-life: run-down plan, final order, clearance
strong_answer_signals: Avoided launch stockouts and EOL excess
avoid: Single replenishment policy for all lifecycle stages

questions.text: Tell me about a time you implemented or improved a Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) process.

key_points: Gap in existing process: misalignment between demand and supply plans
Process design: data inputs, cadence, attendees, decisions
Business outcome: better availability, lower excess, faster decisions

questions.text: How do you calculate safety stock and what factors influence it?

key_points: Formula: Z × σ_demand × √lead_time (demand variability method)
Factors: service level target, demand variability, lead time variability
Dynamic review: adjusts with seasonality or supplier changes
avoid: No variability or service level consideration

questions.text: What is the difference between reorder point and min/max replenishment?

key_points: ROP: trigger order when stock hits demand × lead time + safety stock
Min/max: order up to max when stock falls to min level
Use case: ROP for stable demand; min/max for lumpy or seasonal

questions.text: How do you approach demand forecasting for a highly seasonal product?

key_points: Seasonal index calculation from historical data
Forward-looking inputs: commercial calendar, promotions, market trends
Forecast review cadence increased pre-peak

questions.text: What planning metrics do you track daily and weekly as an inventory planner?

key_points: Daily: stock availability, on-order receipts, stockout alerts
Weekly: days-on-hand by SKU, MAPE, open POs
Monthly: inventory turns, excess/obsolete value, service level
strong_answer_signals: Tiered cadence appropriate to decision horizon

questions.text: How would you approach segmenting your SKU base for inventory planning purposes?

key_points: ABC by revenue/volume, XYZ by demand variability
Combined ABC-XYZ matrix: AX = tight control; CZ = safety stock heavy
Different replenishment policies by segment
avoid: Only ABC with no variability dimension

questions.text: A supplier notifies you of a 6-week delay on a critical component. What do you do?

key_points: Assess stock position vs demand over 6-week gap
Options: alternative supplier, air freight, demand management
Communicate impact to commercial and operations immediately

questions.text: Sales is pushing for higher stock levels on all products to avoid any stockouts. How do you respond?

key_points: Data: show cost of excess vs stockout risk by segment
Targeted approach: increase safety stock only on high-risk, high-value SKUs
Agree on service level by tier and working capital envelope
strong_answer_signals: Cost of capital argument for excess
avoid: Blanket increase with no cost awareness

questions.text: Your forecast system is producing large errors on a new product launch. What do you do?

key_points: New product: system lacks history, override with analogue or commercial estimate
Short review cycle: weekly actuals vs forecast, rapid update
Safety stock elevated during learning phase
strong_answer_signals: Elevated safety stock on new SKU
Weekly forecast review for first 3 months
avoid: Trust statistical model on new product with no history

questions.text: Finance wants to reduce inventory by 25% before year-end. How do you respond without damaging service?

key_points: Model impact of different reduction scenarios on service level
Identify reduction from excess/slow-movers first (no service risk)
Show minimum inventory floor needed to protect service

questions.text: A key product has simultaneous demand spikes from three customers. You do not have enough stock for all. How do you allocate?

key_points: Allocation policy: revenue, strategic value, contractual obligation
Fair and transparent communication to all three customers
Expedite additional supply immediately

questions.text: What draws you to inventory planning as a career?

key_points: Analytical challenge: balancing competing objectives
Tangible business impact: availability and working capital
Cross-functional visibility across the business
strong_answer_signals: Specific to planning not generic supply chain
avoid: No specific aspect of planning articulated

questions.text: How do you stay current with advances in demand planning and inventory optimisation?

key_points: IBF, APICS/ASCM resources and certifications
Tool exploration: Blue Yonder, Kinaxis, o9, Excel modelling
Peer network and industry events

questions.text: How do you develop inventory planners from entry level to independent contributors?

key_points: Structured onboarding: system, data, policy
Stretch assignments with coaching safety net
APICS/CPIM development pathway

questions.text: How do you handle intermittent or lumpy demand patterns in your replenishment model?

key_points: Croston method or similar intermittent demand model
Higher safety stock relative to average demand
Manual review flag for anomaly orders
avoid: Standard moving average applied to lumpy demand

questions.text: Tell me about a time you collaborated with procurement to improve lead time reliability.

key_points: Shared lead time variability data with procurement
Root cause by supplier: capacity, quality, transport
Joint improvement plan with supplier KPI tracking
avoid: Planned around bad lead times without fixing them

questions.text: What is inventory turnover and how do you use it to assess performance?

key_points: Formula: COGS / average inventory value
Benchmark: industry standard by category
Low turns = excess; high turns = stockout risk, both need investigation
strong_answer_signals: Used alongside service level not in isolation

questions.text: Your planning system recommends an order that seems much larger than expected. What do you do before approving it?

key_points: Check forecast input: demand spike or data error
Review parameters: reorder point, safety stock, lead time
Override with documented reason if system error confirmed
strong_answer_signals: Never blind approval of outlier orders

questions.text: Describe a time you managed inventory planning for a product range rationalisation.

key_points: Identified SKUs for discontinuation via contribution and complexity analysis
Run-down plan: final orders, stock allocation, customer communication
Working capital released and planning complexity reduced
strong_answer_signals: Measured outcome: working capital and SKU count
